regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “A STRONGER FOUNDATION FOR KIDNEY PRESERVATION” (page 1) | “Consistent nephroprotection” (pages 1 and 3) | “Achieving complete remission of proteinuria (defined as <0.3 g/d) drives long term nephroprotective benefits” (page 2) | “Kidney Function Preservation” (page 3) | “Proven to achieve better kidney function preservation over 2 years” (page 8) | “FILSPARI®: a stronger foundation for kidney preservation” (page 13)
cases.context: PI indication: 'to slow kidney function decline'; eGFR slope -3.0 vs -4.2 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr vs irbesartan.
cases.rationale: Drug slowed the rate of decline but kidney function still declined, so 'preservation'/'nephroprotection' claims overstate the demonstrated effect.
cases.check: Does the claim describe the outcome more strongly than the labeled effect (e.g., 'preserves/protects' when label says 'slows decline')?

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: a bar graph with the heading “Proven to drive 3x more patients to complete remission of proteinuria (<0.3 g/day)” (page 7) | “Proven to drive 3x more patients to complete remission of proteinuria” (page 13)
cases.context: Footnote disclaimer 'Prespecified exploratory analysis...' acknowledged but does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Complete remission was an exploratory endpoint with no alpha allocated; 'proven' claims are unsupported.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'proven'/'demonstrated' language attached to any endpoint labeled exploratory, post hoc, or not alpha-controlled in the same piece.

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “FILSPARI was well tolerated over 2 years” | “No drug-induced liver injury following treatment with Filspari” in conjunction with an image of a liver
cases.context: Boxed Warnings for hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; REMS with liver monitoring; DILI cases occurred.
cases.rationale: Tolerability and 'no DILI' claims minimize serious boxed-warning risks; risk info elsewhere does not mitigate.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'well tolerated' and 'No [boxed-warning risk]' claims when the product label has a boxed warning or REMS for that risk.

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: a graph depicting mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure over 110 weeks with the headline, “Blood pressure remained consistent over a 2-year period and was comparable to irbesartan”
cases.context: PI W&P: greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events vs irbesartan; hypotension info on pages 10 and 15 does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Implies drug will not adversely affect blood pressure despite labeled hypotension risk.
cases.check: Does a safety/tolerability graphic or headline imply absence of a risk that appears in the label's Warnings and Precautions?
